Introduction
This document out lines the major maintenance 
procedure P1, which must be performed every five years as indication by Y5 in 
the above title block.
This fan function to supply the boiler with combustion air.
Technical specification
The first draft initiated and tested by eng. Gamal Elsyed Osily, reviewed 
by eng. 
Sobhey Abdel Haleem, revised by eng. Samir Abdel Gilil: EDEPC 
 inspection & quality control

Al-Sayed Abdel Ghaffar: general manager of Al-Arish PS

 accepted by eng. Samir Abdel Gilil: EDEPC

 certified by accountant: Mahmoud Soliman EDEPC 
 planning & financial predicting and 
 supervisor of inspection & quality control's head sector.
Safety Precautions
A work order must be issued.
The maintenance staff should be 
 qualified and carry the suitable safety ID category.
Wear safety and healthy equipment as safety helmet, safety 
 shoes etc
Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the work area is required
Isolate the circuit breaker for fan motor.
Unit out of service.
Tools and Equipment
Cleaning fluid, feeler gauge.
Suitable lifting device.
Work to be Carried Out
Before Isolating the FDF 
Mechanically and Electrically
Record the availability of operational data such as vibration level, bearing 
 temperature, motor ampere, damper position etc.
Listen and check any abnormal noise from any components like bearing inlet 
 damper etc.
Observe for any leakage in the fan like oil, water, air at fan connections
After Fan stopped 
and isolated
The following data may be recorded / ensured for reference during reassembly.
Coupling alignment.
Fan shaft level.
Marking the assembled component by match marks.
Disassembly of the 
Coupling figure (1)
Dismantle the safety cover of coupling.
Remove the two covers of coupling away from both.
Then the two shaft can be separated (fan shaft and motor shaft).
Disassembly of the 
Front / Rear Bearing (Sleeve oil Pillow Blocks) figure 2.
Remove temperature sensor.
Disassembly all cooling water pipes (2).
Drain the sump oil by screw off oil drain plug (15).
Screw off the bolts (7), to separate two halves of bearing house.
Screw off plunger screw nut (10) to take liner assemblies out (16).
Disassembly of Impeller 
/ Fan Shaft
Remove all thermometer connections and pipe lines.
Dismount labyrinth seal assemblies.
Remove fasteners in the horizontal and vertical flange joints of upper 
 quadrant of the spiral casing at the discharge end.
Pull and slide out the quadrant remove.
Lift the rotor assembly and position on rotor transport stand with due care.
The impeller can be separated from the shaft by removing the conical cover 
 plate and the shaft flange to impeller connecting bolts.
Inspection after 
assembling
Check the two halves of coupling for mechanical wear.
Check the coupling spring.
Check the two halves of hearing house for mechanical wear.
Check every parts of bearing and liner assembly.
Check the shaft surface finishing and its dimensions at ( bearing seating 
 area, impeller and coupling area ).
Check the impeller and its blades for mechanical wear and tear.
Reassembly
After Inspection
Bearing clearance.
Shaft level.
Impeller clearance.
Fan motor alignment and coupling gap.
Inspection after 
Operation
Measure and record the vibration of fan.
Observe the noise of fan at bearing, inlet damper area.
Check the lube oil level in the front/rear bearing.
Check and record temperature of the front/rear bearing.
Compare the values of vibration and temperature with limits value as shown in the table

Trouble Shooting
Leakage of the water in the 
 bearing liner
Use sealing compound to 
 arrest the leak. If necessary replace liner assembly
Tighten plunger screws to 
 specified torque values.
Improper thermometer
Inadequate lubrication
Inadequate bearing 
 clearance
Improper lub oil
Inadequate cooling
Bearing failure
Mechanical rubbing
Find the fault and rectify
Maintain proper oil level
Set proper bearing 
 clearance. If required replace Bering liners
Ensure use of recommended 
 lub oil
Maintain recommended 
 cooling water flow
Replace the bearing
Find out the part and 
 rectify suitably
Unequal inlet damper 
 setting
Equalize both inlet damper 
 settings
Looseness in damper 
 assembly
Tighten the loose parts and
